answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. Consider a onyx as the anchor of the cost.
